[Become a Member](javascript:void(0))

×

### Associate

**$100** Single membership

100% tax deductible

- Free admission to exhibitions and lecture series
- Access to members-only exhibition hours and preview days
- Domestic travel opportunities
- Free subscription to Muscarelle newsletters
- 20% off exhibition catalogues

[Join or renew · Associate single](https://www.givecampus.com/pgqw2d?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=associate_single) [Associate family · $150 for two](https://www.givecampus.com/pziqzq?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=associate_dual)

### Partner

**$250** Partner membership

100% tax deductible

Includes all Associate benefits, plus:

- Reciprocal membership benefits at more than 600 North American art museums through NARM (North American Reciprocal Museum Association)

[Join or renew · Partner](https://www.givecampus.com/lhrrcg?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=partner)

### Sustainer

**$500** Sustainer membership

100% tax deductible

Includes all Partner benefits, plus:

- Reciprocal membership benefits at more than 100 museums in the Southeast through SEMC (Southeastern Museums Conference)
- One private docent-led tour for up to six guests
- Early registration access for Muscarelle Members’ Events

[Join or renew · Sustainer](https://www.givecampus.com/ysumkc?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=sustainer)

[Give a membership](https://www.givecampus.com/vns2yo?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=gift_membership)

Show additional membership levels Hide additional membership levels

### Patron Circle

**$1,000**

Tax-deductible portion: $935

Includes all Sustainer benefits, plus:

- Two private docent-led tours for up to six guests
- Invitation to VIP Members’ openings
- Invitation to an annual Patron’s Dinner with the Director

[Join or renew · Patron Circle](https://www.givecampus.com/spshz9?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=patron_circle)

### Curator’s Circle

**$2,500**

Tax-deductible portion: $2,435

Includes all Patron Circle benefits, plus:

- Membership in William & Mary’s Fourth Century Society, with eligibility for all Society recognition opportunities\*
- Invitation to participate in an exclusive curatorial selection project

[Join or renew · Curator’s Circle](https://www.givecampus.com/a5pe8c?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=curators_circle)

### Director’s Circle

**$5,000**

Tax-deductible portion: $4,870

Includes all Curator’s Circle benefits, plus:

- Membership in William & Mary’s President’s Society, with eligibility for all President’s Society recognition opportunities\*
- Invitation to the Muscarelle Director’s Dinner and a behind-the-scenes tour

[Join or renew · Director’s Circle](https://www.givecampus.com/wow6sm?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=directors_circle)

### Lamberson & Muscarelle Circles

#### Lamberson Circle

**$10,000**

Tax-deductible portion: $9,870

Includes all Director’s Circle benefits, plus:

- Membership in W&M’s Green & Gold Society, with eligibility for all Society-level recognition opportunities\*
- Invitations to exclusive Director’s events

[Join or renew · Lamberson Circle](https://www.givecampus.com/b3vuqs?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=lamberson_circle)

#### Muscarelle Circle

**$25,000**

Tax-deductible portion: $24,870

Includes all Lamberson Circle benefits, plus:

- Membership in William & Mary’s Chancellor’s Society, with eligibility for all Society-level recognition opportunities\*

[Join or renew · Muscarelle Circle](https://www.givecampus.com/ibx575?utm_source=musce&utm_medium=web&utm_campaign=muscarelle_circle)

## 1996-2026

## Celebrating 30 years of Art, Access, and Education.

Founded in 1981 as the Center of Contemporary Art, our museum began as an artist-centered space and has since grown into a cultural anchor for South Florida through 30 years of visionary leadership. With support from the City of North Miami, founding director Lou Anne Colodny inaugurated the Charles Gwathmey–designed building that houses the museum today. Opened in 1996, it marked the institution’s transition to the Museum of Contemporary Art North Miami (MOCA). Following suit, Bonnie Clearwater ushered in a transformative era, bringing world-renowned artists into the galleries through her rigorous curatorial projects. Together with founding Chair Richard Shack, the board of trustees, and these pioneering women, MOCA’s early success was cemented. 

[Explore our Timeline](https://www.mocanomi.org/timeline)

## Learn at MOCA

Ages 1 - 5

### Sunday Stories

Tune in on the first Sunday of every month for MOCA's Sunday Stories, a live story time for children, followed by a DIY early childhood art project.

[Learn More](https://www.mocanomi.org/learn/children)

Ages 6 - 12

### MiniMakers

Join us every first Saturday of the month for MOCA miniMakers , a free step-by-step art making experience for kids.

[Learn More](https://www.mocanomi.org/learn/minimakers)

Ages 13 - 17

### Teen Art Force

A free after-school art program that provides students with a foundation in the visual arts. Classes include a wide range of techniques including drawing, textile design, sculpture, and printmaking.

[Learn More](https://www.mocanomi.org/learn/teens)

Ages 18+

### MOCA Makers

Free adult art classes taught by trained professional artists, offered every second Saturday of the month.

[Learn More](https://www.mocanomi.org/learn/adults)

### En el corazón de Santurce, el MAPR reúne arte puertorriqueño desde el siglo XVIII hasta el presente. Descubre la colección, disfruta las exhibiciones, explora el Jardín Escultórico y conecta con el arte y la cultura.

[¡Planifica tu visita!](https://mapr.org/planifica-tu-visita/)

# Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University

[Dark-toned painting of a crowded gathering, with faceless figures outlined in warm lines and accented by muted blues, reds, and greens.](https://nasher.duke.edu/exhibitions/turn-the-volume-up/)

## [We the People](https://nasher.duke.edu/exhibitions/we-the-people/)

[slide 3of6 Large, expressive painting of figures gathered in and around a tree-like form, with people seated along its branches and a crowd below in a hazy landscape.](https://nasher.duke.edu/exhibitions/contemporary-british-art/)

On View Now | July 18, 2026 – September 12, 2027

## [Contemporary British Art](https://nasher.duke.edu/exhibitions/contemporary-british-art/)

[slide 4of6 a painting os a boxer lifting another boxer over his shoulder](https://nasher.duke.edu/exhibitions/tall-tales-and-short-stories/)

On View Now | September 08 – December 06, 2026

## [Read the Room: R.B. Kitaj’s IN OUR TIME Today](https://nasher.duke.edu/exhibitions/read-the-room/)

[drummers playing outside the Nasher Museum.](https://nasher.duke.edu/giving__trashed/annual-fund-gifts/)

## [Donate Today!](https://nasher.duke.edu/giving__trashed/annual-fund-gifts/)

Your support of the Nasher directly fuels free admission, inspiring public programs, and vibrant community events.

[Give today](https://nasher.duke.edu/giving/annual-fund-gifts/).

[in the foreground, a photograph of a woman in front of an American flag is hanging on a wall that ends in the middle of the image. In the background, two visitors walk past more artwork on the wall behind.](https://nasher.duke.edu/visitor-info/hours-admission/)

## [Free Admission](https://nasher.duke.edu/visitor-info/hours-admission/)

Enjoy free entry every day — check hours and plan your visit.

Courtesy of [Jennifer McCracken New & Jason New](https://nasher.duke.edu/stories/nasher-museum-receives-1-million-gift-to-offer-free-admission-for-all/).

[a drone image of the Nasher Museum](https://nasher.duke.edu/mission/)

## [Mission](https://nasher.duke.edu/mission/)

The Nasher Museum of Art at Duke University amplifies untold stories, creates space for exchange, and invites shared experiences through innovative exhibitions and programs. Embedded in a leading research university, the museum serves as a laboratory for ambitious experimentation and the generation of new knowledge and open dialogue. We intentionally partner with our communities to foster curiosity and wonder through the visual arts.

# Reimagining the MFA Collection

The MFA is beginning an exciting transformation called Art Unbound. This is a multi-phase project that will reimagine how you experience the museum, from the collection galleries to transitional spaces and the outdoor campus.

Rather than simply presenting art by date or geographic region, the updated collection galleries will explore universal human themes and bring works from different cultures and time periods into conversation with one another.

The MFA collection will be closed for a few months during this reimagination.

[LEARN MORE](https://mfastpete.org/about/reimagination/)

### EXPLORE THE WORLD. CHOOSE YOUR ADVENTURE.

Welcome to the Museum of Fine Arts, St. Petersburg, where art and culture meet. As a community hub in the heart of downtown St. Petersburg, the MFA offers a diverse collection of world-class art, immersive exhibitions, and inspiring programs for all ages.

## EXPERIENCE THE MFA 
IN THE PALM OF YOUR HAND

Go beyond the frame with our free digital guide on the **Bloomberg Connects app**. Access exclusive audio tours and expert insights that bring our world-class collection to life—right from your own device. It is the perfect companion to help you explore before, during, or after your visit.

[LEARN MORE](https://mfastpete.org/freedigitalguide/)

## BE A PART OF THE ART

Margaret Acheson Stuart founded the first art museum in St. Petersburg with the support of those who believed in the transformative power of art. Today, the Museum of Fine Arts stands as a cultural cornerstone for the entire community.

As a not-for-profit institution, the MFA relies on diverse funding to offer arts-integrated education programs and showcase innovative exhibitions. For decades, countless individuals have supported Mrs. Stuart’s commitment to the arts through memberships, Annual Fund contributions, and volunteering.

We are deeply grateful to our members and donors, whose vital support makes it all possible. Join us in continuing this legacy of art and education. Donate today.

Neuberger Museum of Art

# Neuberger Museum of Art

## Who NEU? The Neuberger's _Barber Shop_ is the largest painting ever created by Edward Hopper

## **Welcome!**

The Neuberger Museum of Art is a vibrant hub of creativity, learning, and inspiration for all ages! Located at the heart of SUNY Purchase, our Museum invites you to explore breathtaking exhibitions of modern, contemporary, and African art, along with dynamic events that spark thought and conversation.

Founded in 1969 with a generous gift of 300 works from Roy R. Neuberger, a pioneering philanthropist and arts advocate, our collection has expanded to nearly 7,000 objects. Here, you’ll encounter masterpieces by renowned artists such as Milton Avery, Romare Bearden, Alexander Calder, Stuart Davis, Helen Frankenthaler, Marsden Hartley, Edward Hopper, Georgia O’Keeffe, Louise Nevelson, Jackson Pollock, Hedda Sterne, Rufino Tamayo, Max Weber, and Zao Wou-Ki alongside objects by living artists including Chakaia Booker, the Guerrilla Girls, and Judy Pfaff, to name just a few.

We also honor exceptional contemporary artists with the **Roy R. Neuberger Prize**, continuing our founder’s commitment to supporting emerging talent and making art accessible to all.

Beyond our permanent collection, we offer critically acclaimed [exhibitions](https://www.purchase.edu/neuberger-museum-of-art/exhibitions/) that attract visitors from near and far. Whether you’re a student, educator, artist, or art lover, our engaging [events](https://www.purchase.edu/neuberger-museum-of-art/events/) — including tours, lectures, and programs — are designed to inspire, challenge, and connect our diverse community.

Our [members](https://www.purchase.edu/neuberger-museum-of-art/join/) play a vital role in sustaining the museum’s mission, supporting our vision of showcasing global contemporary artists, fostering arts education, and creating a space for exploration and growth.

At the Neuberger Museum of Art, the possibilities are endless. Come join us, experiment, question, and grow through the transformative power of art.

Explore these pages and follow us @neubergermuseum

## **Our Mission**

The Neuberger Museum of Art, SUNY Purchase, champions those who make art, engage with art, and discover meaning through art.

## Our Vision

The Neuberger Museum of Art, SUNY Purchase, is a creative community. Its renowned collection, exhibitions, and education programming focus on the art of today and of the recent past to promote learning and engagement for people of all ages and backgrounds.

## Our Values

The SUNY Purchase values that inspire and guide the Museum’s work:

- Excellence in museum practice
- Delivery of exceptional education experiences
- Artistic and scholarly achievement
- Personal and professional creativity, inquiry, and expressiveness
- Openness to emerging ideas that promote alternatives and variance
- Free and expressive speech
- Diversity, equity, and inclusion
- Respect for individuals’ liberties
- Lifelong learning
- Meaningful collaboration toward shared goals
- Civic engagement
- Sustainability 

[Read Our Strategic Plan](https://www.purchase.edu/neuberger-museum-of-art/strategic-plan/)

# National Museum of Women in the Arts

### Now on View

Visit NMWA to view _Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California_, featuring nearly 80 artworks with kaleidoscopic patterns, colors, and forms, offering a history of art through quilts’ joyful power in Black life.

[Learn More About NMWA’s Current Exhibitions](https://nmwa.org/whats-on/exhibitions/)  

## Visit Us

The National Museum of Women in the Arts is the first museum in the world dedicated solely to championing women through the arts. Located in the heart of Washington, DC, at 1250 New York Ave. NW, just steps from Metro Center. NMWA is open Tuesday through Sunday and welcomes visitors of all ages.

[Plan Your Visit](https://nmwa.org/visit/plan-your-visit/)  

Photo by Derek Baker for NMWA

## Current Exhibitions

### Routed West

Featuring nearly 80 artworks by more than 70 individuals, _Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California_ threads the needle between Black people’s historical movements and their quilts to tell stories of collective care, resilience, and creativity

[View Routed West](https://nmwa.org/exhibitions/routed-west-twentieth-century-african-american-quilts-in-california/)  

### Marlo Pascual

Featuring 17 works, _Marlo Pascual: Making Something Out of Something_ demonstrates the artist’s methods of recontextualization. Blurring the boundaries between photography and sculpture, Pascual transforms what is familiar into something uncanny, prompting deeper contemplation.

[View Marlo Pascual](https://nmwa.org/exhibitions/marlo-pascual-making-something-out-of-something/)  

### Beverly Pepper

Featuring maquettes for large-scale works and a new film about the groundbreaking sculptor, _Beverly Pepper: Land Art and Monumental Sculptures_ complements an installation of ten monumental sculptures by Pepper, on view just outside NMWA’s entrance.

[View Beverly Pepper](https://nmwa.org/exhibitions/beverly-pepper-land-art-and-monumental-sculptures/)  

### Remix

_Remix: The Collection_ showcases familiar collection favorites as well as never-before-exhibited recent acquisitions. Artworks are grouped around themes that resonate among global artists across time.

[View Remix](https://nmwa.org/exhibitions/remix-the-collection/)

## What We Do

Our rotating special exhibitions showcase historic and contemporary artwork. Museum programs and events foster conversations and connections that inspire change. Our collections feature more than 6,500 works from the 16th century to today created by more than 1,000 artists.

> People in the art world want to think we are achieving parity more quickly than we are.”

Susan Fisher Sterling, The Alice West Director

## Advocate for Gender Equity

Historically, social and cultural systems based on false beliefs about gender have hindered artists’ power, access, and agency. Gender bias is less overt today, but contemporary women artists still face many obstacles and disparities, as well as persistent underrepresentation in museum collections and exhibitions worldwide.

## Plan Your Visit to NOMA

# New Orleans Museum of Art

### Tuesday–Sunday, 10 am–5 pm; Wednesdays, 12–7 pm

Explore art from around the world—dating from ancient times to present day. The museum’s permanent collection and exhibitions span three floors.

[Visitor Information](https://noma.org/visit/visitor-information/)

_Admission is free for Louisiana residents every Wednesday, courtesy of The Helis Foundation’s Art for All initiative._

# Sydney and Walda Besthoff Sculpture Garden

### Free and open to all, seven days a week

Where art meets nature—experience 100 works of art set in a unique Louisiana landscape.

[Learn More](https://noma.org/besthoff-sculpture-garden/)

## During Your Visit

# NOMA Museum Shop

### Open during regular museum hours and programs

Discover a rotating selection of artful books, gifts, jewelry, and more inspired by what’s on view at NOMA. Take home catalogues for your favorite exhibitions, special collaborations with local artists, and creative activities for all ages.

[Shop Online](https://shop.noma.org/)

# Café NOMA by Ralph Brennan

### Tuesday–Sunday, 10 am–4 pm; Wednesdays: 11 am–7 pm

Enjoy pastries, coffee, lunch, cocktails, and more daily—set against the dramatic backdrop of over 90 objects from NOMA’s permanent collection highlighting global food and dining culture.

[Learn More](https://www.cafenoma.com/)

_Stop by Café NOMA for happy hour on Wednesdays, 3–6 pm, for drink specials and shareable small plates._

### [New Orleans Museum of Art to Present _Marie Antoinette Style_ in 2027](https://noma.org/new-orleans-museum-of-art-to-present-marie-antoinette-style-in-2027/)

[Read More](https://noma.org/new-orleans-museum-of-art-to-present-marie-antoinette-style-in-2027/)

### [Educator Guide for _Second Nature: Japanese Rinpa Paintings from the Gitter-Yelen Collection_ Now Available Online for Free](https://noma.org/educator-guide-for-second-nature-japanese-rinpa-paintings-from-the-gitter-yelen-collection-now-available-online-for-free/)

A free and downloadable Educator's Guide to "Second Nature: Japanese Rinpa Paintings from the Gitter-Yelen Collection," on view at NOMA now through February 14, 2027, is now available. 
[Read More](https://noma.org/educator-guide-for-second-nature-japanese-rinpa-paintings-from-the-gitter-yelen-collection-now-available-online-for-free/)

### [Announcing the 2026–27 Creative Assembly Cohort](https://noma.org/announcing-the-2026-27-creative-assembly-cohort/)

This year’s cohort of Creative Assembly residents at the New Orleans Museum of Art (NOMA) includes six artists working in painting, music, poetry, film, and other disciplines.  
[Read More](https://noma.org/announcing-the-2026-27-creative-assembly-cohort/)

NOMA members receive unlimited admission to the museum, as well as reduced ticket prices to programs and events, discounts in the NOMA Museum Shop, invitations to member-exclusive programs, and more

As the first museum dedicated to acquiring American Art in the country, the New Britain Museum of American Art’s collection contains more than 9,000 works representing over three centuries of major artists and movements of American Art.

[ABOUT THE COLLECTION](https://nbmaa.org/permanent-collection)

[nbmaa56](https://www.instagram.com/nbmaa56/)

A young woman reclines on a couch, absorbed in thought. The sitter is the artist's daughter, Frances Frieseke, who frequently modeled for her father. Painted in 1936 at the family's home in Normandy, the work reflects a shift in Frederick Carl Frieseke's art. Earlier in his career, he was celebrated for luminous Impressionist scenes filled with sunlight, color, and decorative patterns. By the 1930s, however, his work had become more subdued and contemplative. The still pose, restrained palette, and sense of introspection give "Girl on Couch" a quiet emotional weight, transforming the familiar domestic scene into a deeply personal portrait. 

This painting is now on view at the New Britain Museum of American Art in the Douglas K.S. Hyland Gallery. 

🎨Frederick Carl Frieseke, "Girl on Couch," 1936, Oil on canvas, 26 1/2 x 32 in., Charles and Elizabeth Buchanan Collection, 1989.2

## Discover our artworks.

Our extraordinary collection brings together centuries of masterpieces from around the world. 

[Explore by artist, topic, period, and more](https://www.nga.gov/artworks)

[**Play Color Catch on Roblox**\\ \\ Dash through worlds inspired by our artworks in this interactive game of chase.](https://www.nga.gov/fun-and-games/roblox-color-catch)

## A few of our favorites

[This painting shows a woman sitting with her body turned to the right, her hands clasped around her knees and her head tilted up to the ceiling. Her eyes are closed, and her long, wavy hair flows over her shoulders and down her back. She has pale skin, and her face is illuminated by dramatic lighting, highlighting her round cheeks and small nose. She is wearing a white blouse with ruffled sleeves that drapes off of her right shoulder, exposing her neck, sternum, and part of her shoulder. Over this shirt she seems to be wearing a draped purple garment with a yellow border that covers her other shoulder and her legs. The background is dark.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/231465-mary-magdalene-ecstasy)

Artemisia Gentileschi, [Mary Magdalene in Ecstasy](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/231465-mary-magdalene-ecstasy), c. 1625, oil on canvas, Gift of Funds from Nina J. Cohen in honor of her father Emanuel Cohen and Patrons' Permanent Fund, 2025.88.1

[We look out onto a sweeping, panoramic view with trees, their leaves fiery orange and red, framing a view of a distant body of water under a sun-streaked sky in this long, horizontal landscape painting. The horizon comes about halfway up the composition, and is lined with hazy mountains and clouds in the deep distance. Close examination slowly reveals minuscule birds tucked into the crimson-red, golden yellow, and deep, sage-green leaves of the trees to either side of the painting. Closest to us, vine-covered, fallen tree trunks and mossy gray boulders line the bottom edge of the canvas. Beyond a trickling waterfall and small pool near the lower left corner, and tiny within the scale of the landscape, a group of three men and their dogs sit and recline around a blanket and a picnic basket, their rifles leaning against a tree nearby. The land sweeps down to a grassy meadow crossed by a meandering stream that winds into the distance, at the center of the painting. Touches of white and gray represent a flock of grazing sheep in the meadow. A low wooden bridge spans the stream to our right, and a few cows drink from the riverbank. Smoke rises from chimneys in a town lining the riverbank and shoreline beyond, and tiny white sails and steamboats dot the waterway. Light pours onto the scene with rays like a starburst from behind a lavender-gray cloud covering the sun, low in the sky. The artist signed the painting as if he had inscribed the flat top of a rock at the lower center of the landscape with his name, the title of the painting, and date: “Autumn – on the Hudson River, J.F Cropsey, London 1860.”](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/46474-autumn-hudson-river)

Jasper Francis Cropsey, [Autumn - On the Hudson River](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/46474-autumn-hudson-river), 1860, oil on canvas, Gift of the Avalon Foundation, 1963.9.1

[At the top of this painting is a smooth, dark shape resembling a bird in flight. The bird is made of long, curved lines, with its wings extended to either side and its head pointing to the left. The background of the painting is a blue gradient, transitioning from a medium blue at the top to a very light, almost-white shade of blue in the middle of the painting. The very bottom of the painting is completely white and forms a U-shaped valley below the bird.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/204792-black-bird-snow-covered-red-hills)

Georgia O'Keeffe, [A Black Bird with Snow-Covered Red Hills](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/204792-black-bird-snow-covered-red-hills), 1946, oil on canvas, Anonymous Gift, 2021.58.1

[Six women, eight men, two satyrs, and one child gather in pairs and trios in a loose row that spans the width of this nearly square painting. They are set within a landscape with craggy rocks, cliffs, and trees. Most of the people face us, and the men, women, and child have pale skin. The two satyrs have men’s torsos and furry goat’s legs, and they have darker, olive complexions. Most of the men wear voluminous, knee-length togas wrapped in short robes in shades of white, topaz blue, grass green, coral orange, or rose pink. Most of the women wear long, dress-like garments in tones of shell pink, apricot orange, or lapis blue over white sleeves. For all but one woman, their garments have fallen off one shoulder to reveal a round, firm breast. Several objects are strewn on the rocky, dirt ground in front of the group, including a wide, wooden bucket with a piece of paper affixed to its front to our right, a glass goblet, a pitchfork, a large blue and white ceramic dish filled with grapes and small yellow fruits, and an overturned cup near the center. Cliff-like, craggy rocks rise steeply behind the group to our left, filling much of the sky opposite a tall grove of leafy, dark green trees to our right. A few puffy white clouds float across the vivid blue sky. The slip of paper on the barrel has been inscribed, “joannes bellinus venetus p MDXIIII.”](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/1138-feast-gods)

Giovanni Bellini, Titian, [The Feast of the Gods](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/1138-feast-gods), 1514/1529, oil on canvas, Widener Collection, 1942.9.1

[The top quarter of this horizontal abstract painting is dominated by bright, sunshine yellow over areas of sky blue, moss and forest green, and white below. The painting is made up of four vertical panels joined to make one long composition. Yellow dominates the leftmost panel over a field of pale blue marked with forest and spring green, teal, and yellow, mostly along the bottom edge of the canvas. The field of pale blue and white take up most of the space in the two center panels, with a band of yellow above and deep green marks below. In the rightmost panel, the blue field is more variegated with darker blues, shades of green, white, and yellow. Throughout, some of the colors are layered and sometimes they are applied next to each other. Thick and thin areas of paint and drips create a variety of textures on the surface of each panel. The artist signed this work in pencil in the lower right corner: “Joan Mitchell.”](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/195052-salut-tom)

Joan Mitchell, [Salut Tom](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/195052-salut-tom), 1979, oil on canvas, Corcoran Collection (Gift of the Women's Committee of the Corcoran Gallery of Art, and Museum Purchase with the aid of funds from the National Endowment for the Arts, 1979), 2014.136.135

[In this vertical painting, a woman stands near the corner of a dimly lit room, facing our left in profile and looking down at a balance she holds suspended in her right hand over a wooden table. She wears a peacock-blue velvet jacket with a white hood and fur lining, and a voluminous, mustard-yellow skirt. A window near the upper left corner is partially covered by a canary-yellow curtain. Light coming in through that window falls on the pale skin of the woman's face and hands, and highlights the white trim of her garment. Her left hand, closer to us, rests on the edge of the table near two open boxes, and a blue cloth is bunched at the back of the table to our left. Gold chains and pearl strands drape over the edge of one box. The woman stands in front of a framed painting. Much of the detail is lost in shadow but at the top center of the painting, a person surrounded by a golden halo floats in the sky with both arms raised, and is flanked by people encased within a bank of clouds. Nude people on the ground below in the painting, seen to either side of the woman, writhe, twist, and point upward.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/1236-woman-holding-balance)

Johannes Vermeer, [Woman Holding a Balance](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/1236-woman-holding-balance), c. 1664, oil on canvas, Widener Collection, 1942.9.97

Edgar Degas, [Little Dancer Aged Fourteen](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/110292-little-dancer-aged-fourteen), 1878-1881, pigmented beeswax, clay, metal armature, rope, paintbrushes, human hair, silk and linen ribbon, cotton faille bodice, cotton and silk tutu, linen slippers, on wooden base, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, 1999.80.28

[Shown from the knees up, a woman with brown, wrinkled skin, wearing a white blouse, apron, and black skirt is shown in front of a pale gray background in this vertical portrait painting. Straight-backed, she faces and looks at us with her hands resting in her lap. Her wavy, iron-gray hair is parted in the center and pulled back from her face. Her eyebrows are slightly raised, and her face is deeply lined down her cheeks and around her mouth. She wears a heart-shaped brooch with a red stone at its center at her neck and a gold band on her left ring finger. The light coming from our left casts a shadow against the wall to our right. The artist signed and dated the painting in the lower right corner: “A.J. MOTLEY. JR. 1922.”](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/206066-portrait-my-grandmother)

Archibald John Motley Jr., [Portrait of My Grandmother](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/206066-portrait-my-grandmother), 1922, oil on canvas, Patrons' Permanent Fund, Avalon Fund, and Motley Fund, 2018.2.1

[This square portrait shows the head and shoulders of a young woman in front of a spiky bush that fills much of the background except for a landscape view that extends into the deep distance to our right. The woman's body is angled to our right but her face turns to us. She has chalk-white, smooth skin with heavily lidded, light brown eyes, and her pale pink lips are closed. Pale blush highlights her cheeks, and she looks either at us or very slightly away from our eyes. Her brown hair is parted down the middle and pulled back, but tight, lively curls frame her face. Her hair turns gold where the light shines on it. She wears a brown dress, trimmed along the square neckline with gold. The front of the bodice is tied with a blue ribbon, and the lacing holes are also edged with gold. A sheer white veil covers her chest and is pinned at the center with a small gold ball. The bush fills the space around her head with copper-brown, spiky leaves. A river winds between trees and rolling hills in the distance to our right. Trees and a town along the horizon, which comes about halfway up the painting, is pale blue under an ice-blue sky.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/50724-ginevra-de-benci-obverse)

Leonardo da Vinci, [Ginevra de' Benci \[obverse\]](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/50724-ginevra-de-benci-obverse), c. 1474/1478, oil on panel, Ailsa Mellon Bruce Fund, 1967.6.1.a

[The image shows a misty view of Mount Rushmore, focusing on the natural landscape surrounding the monument. The point of view is slightly upward, capturing the rugged terrain and dense forest leading up to the mountain. The horizon is obscured by low clouds and mist that cover the top of the mountain. The color palette includes earthy tones of green from the pine trees and gray from the rocky slopes, with the fog adding a soft, muted quality to the scene. The monument is partially visible, with the sculpted faces emerging from the rock face, blending with the natural surroundings.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/231756-mount-rushmore-national-memorial-six-grandfathers-south-dakota-2018)

Mitch Epstein, [Mount Rushmore National Memorial, Six Grandfathers, South Dakota 2018](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/231756-mount-rushmore-national-memorial-six-grandfathers-south-dakota-2018), 2018, printed 2025, inkjet print, Gift of the Artist, © Mitch Epstein, 2025.70.3

[A man with pale peach skin and dark hair wears a military uniform and stands in front of a desk in this vertical portrait painting. He nearly fills the composition so seems close to us, and he looks directly at us. His body is angled slightly to our left and he tucks his right hand, on our left, flat against his chest between the buttons of his jacket. His navy-blue waistcoat is white along the front where it is fastened with brass buttons along his chest. The jacket has red cuffs, gold epaulets on the shoulders, and three medals affixed to the chest. White britches end just below the knee, and white stockings covering his calves are wrinkled at the ankle above black shoes with brass buckles. A candle burns low in a lamp on an ornately carved and gilded desk behind the man. Books and papers are piled on the desk to our right. More papers and a thin sword rest on a chair in front of the desk to our right. The chair is also carved and gilded, and is upholstered with scarlet-red fabric decorated with gold bees. The legs of the chair push back the forest-green carpet underfoot. A tall clock stands on the wall opposite us and reads 4:13. A few capital letters are written on a scroll of paper on the chair, “COD.” The artist’s name is also written as if printed on a scroll of paper on the floor behind the desk to our left: “LVD.CI.DAVID OPVS 1812.”](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/46114-emperor-napoleon-his-study-tuileries)

Jacques-Louis David, [The Emperor Napoleon in His Study at the Tuileries](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/46114-emperor-napoleon-his-study-tuileries), 1812, oil on canvas, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 1961.9.15

[This painting shows a grand city square filled with people. There are two long white buildings on the left and right of the square, both with large arched windows, smaller round windows, columns, and several rows of balconies. Every balcony and window is filled with people. Between the two buildings, to the right of center, is a domed structure with three tiered layers comprised of central arched openings surrounded by columns topped with statues and covered with intricate railings and details. The square is filled with people in long coats, dresses or pants, and hats, all in shades of gray. Most of them face away from us, looking towards the center of the square where performers stand on a stage, arranged in a pyramid formation using thin beams. The sky above is a gradient of gray, suggesting a cloud-filled sky.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/139341-giovedi-grasso-festival-ducal-palace-venice)

Canaletto, [The "Giovedì Grasso" Festival before the Ducal Palace in Venice](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/139341-giovedi-grasso-festival-ducal-palace-venice), 1765/1766, pen and brown ink with gray wash over traces of graphite, tip of the brush with black wash, heightened with touches of white gouache (laid on thick eighteenth-century mount), Wolfgang Ratjen Collection, Paul Mellon Fund, 2007.111.55

[Two women with pale skin look out at us from the other side of a rectangular window opening with a shadowy interior behind them in this vertical painting. On our right, in the lower third of the composition, one young woman leans toward us over her left arm, which rests along the window ledge. She bends her right arm and props her chin on her fist. She looks at us with dark brown eyes under dark brows. She has shiny chestnut-brown hair with a strawberry-red bow on the right side of her head, to our left. She has a straight nose, and her full pink lips curve up in a smile. She wears a gossamer-white dress with a wide neckline trimmed in dark gray, with another red bow on the front of her chest. Her voluminous sleeves are pushed back to her elbows. To our left, a second woman peeks around a partially opened shutter. She is slightly older, and she stands next to the first woman with her body facing us. She tilts her head and also gazes at us with dark eyes under dark brown brows. She has dark brown hair covered by an oyster-white shawl. She holds the shawl up with her right hand to cover the bottom half of her face. Her mouth is hidden but her eyes crinkle as if in a smile. Her left arm bends at the elbow as she grasps the open shutter. She also wears a white shirt pushed back to her elbows, and a rose-pink skirt. The frame of the window runs parallel to the sides and bottom of the canvas. The room behind them is black in shadow.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/1185-two-women-window)

Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, [Two Women at a Window](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/1185-two-women-window), c. 1655/1660, oil on canvas, Widener Collection, 1942.9.46

[A small brown dog and a pale-skinned little girl wearing a white dress sit in matching celestial-blue armchairs in this horizontal painting. To our right, the girl sits with her legs angled to our left. She slumps back with her legs spread, and her left elbow, on our right, is bent so that hand rests behind her head. Her other elbow is draped over the armrest. Her dark brown hair appears to be pulled back, and tawny brown eyes under faint brows gaze down and to our left. She has a small nose set in a round face and a coral-pink mouth closed in a straight line. Her white dress has touches of gray, soft pink, and powder blue with a wide plaid sash around her waist. The pine-green, black, and sapphire-blue sash is accented with overlapping vertical and horizontal lines of burnt orange, light blue, and mustard yellow. Her socks match her sash and come up to mid-calf, over black shoes with silver buckles. The small dog has scruffy black fur and a russet-brown face. It lies curled in the chair opposite the girl, to our left, with its eyes closed and ears pricked up. The rounded backs of the upholstered chairs curve down to become the low arms. The vivid and light blue fabric of the chairs is scattered with loosely painted strokes of avocado and forest green, peach pink, cherry red, plum purple, and white. Beyond the chairs closest to us is another armchair and an armless loveseat, both covered with the same fabric. They sit at the back of the room, in a corner flooded with silvery light coming through four windows on the right side. The furniture is arranged on a peanut-brown floor. The artist signed in the lower left, “Mary Cassatt.”](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/61368-little-girl-blue-armchair)

Mary Cassatt, [Little Girl in a Blue Armchair](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/61368-little-girl-blue-armchair), 1878, oil on canvas, Collection of Mr. and Mrs. Paul Mellon, 1983.1.18

[We look onto the side of a rowboat crowded with nine men trying to save a pale, nude young man who flails in the water in front of us as a shark approaches, mouth agape, from our right in this horizontal painting. In the water, the man floats with his chest facing the sky, his right arm overhead and the other stretched out by his side. Extending to our left, his left leg is bent and the right leg is straight, disappearing below the knee. His long blond hair swirls in the water and he arches his back, his wide-open eyes looking toward the shark behind him. To our right, the shark rolls up out of the water with its gaping jaws showing rows of pointed teeth. In the boat, eight of the men have light or tanned complexions, and one man has dark brown skin. The man with brown skin stands at the back center of the boat, and he holds one end of a rope, which falls across the boat and around the upper arm of the man in the water. Another man stands at the stern of the boat, to our right, poised with a long, hooked harpoon over the side of the boat, ready to strike the shark. His long dark hair blows back and he wears a navy-blue jacket with brass buttons, white breeches, blue stockings, and his shoes have silver buckles. Two other men wearing white shirts with blousy sleeves lean over the side of the boat, bracing each other as they reach toward the man in the water. An older, balding man holds the shirt and body of one of this pair and looks on, his mouth open. The other men hold long oars and look into the water with furrowed brows. The tip of a shark’s tail slices through the water to our right of the boat, near the right edge of the canvas. Along the horizon line, which comes three-quarters of the way up the composition, buildings and tall spires line the harbor. The masts of boats at port creates a row of crosses against the light blue sky. Steely gray clouds sweep across the upper left corner of the canvas and the sky lightens to pale, butter yellow at the horizon.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/46471-watson-and-shark)

John Singleton Copley, [Watson and the Shark](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/46471-watson-and-shark), 1778, oil on canvas, Ferdinand Lammot Belin Fund, 1963.6.1

[Carved from creamy white marble, a nude woman stands next to a hip-high support, perhaps a low post. In this photograph, her body faces us, and she looks down to our right in profile. Her wavy hair is tucked behind her ear and drawn back in a bun at the nape of her neck. Her weight rests on her left leg, on our right, and her other knee is bent. Her left arm is angled in front of her body so her hand covers her groin. Her other hand, on our left, rests on the post. Chains hang from shackles encircling her wrists. The post is covered with a cloth that gathers around the top and spirals to the ground beneath her feet, the edge trimmed with tassels. A cross and medallion peek out from under the cloth near her hand. She stands on a circular base.](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/166484-greek-slave)

Hiram Powers, [The Greek Slave](https://www.nga.gov/artworks/166484-greek-slave), model 1841-1843, carved 1846, Seravezza marble, Corcoran Collection (Gift of William Wilson Corcoran, 1873), 2014.79.37

40th Anniversary

# Arts. Nature. People.

## Welcome

Welcoming over 1.1 million visitors to our campus every year and supporting arts programming across all 100 counties of North Carolina, we are more than a museum. We are _your_ art museum. 

**HOURS**

| Museum Store, Wednesday – Sunday, 10 am–5 pm |

[Plan Your Visit](http://ncartmuseum.org/plan-your-visit)

[About the Museum](http://ncartmuseum.org/about)

## Plan Your Visit

- ### Buildings

 From temporary exhibitions to the permanent People’s Collection, our buildings house over 5,000 years of arts and culture.

 [Visit](https://ncartmuseum.org/digital-maps-and-gallery-portals/)

- ### The Museum Park

 Enjoy 4.7 miles of trails, public art, gardens, and outdoor experiences in the Ann and Jim Goodnight Museum Park.

 [Visit](https://ncartmuseum.org/plan-your-visit/museum-park/)

## Tickets

Admission to the People’s Collection and Museum Park are free. Your generosity makes a difference. Whether through membership, a donation, gift, or sponsorship, your help supports art and programming on our campus and across our state.

## Events This Week

- [**Educator Online Course: Art and SEL**\\ \\ In this self-paced 15-hour course, educators explore an arts-based approach to social emotional learning through themes of Mindfulness, Identity, Perspective Sharing, Community Building, and Agency. They participate in experiences that model growth and development of justice-oriented, global citizens.  A certificate of participation for 15 hours will be provided (1.5 CEU, with approval from the local school system). This course was developed in collaboration with the Friday Institute for Educational Innovation.  Image: Luis Rey Velasco, Confirmation, Raising of the Candles, 2005, gelatin silver print, 8 1/2 × 12 3/4 in., Purchased with funds from the William R. Roberson Jr. and Frances M. Roberson Endowed Fund for North Carolina Art \\ \\ October 6, 2026 – December 8, 2026](https://ncartmuseum.org/event/educator-online-course-art-and-sel/)
- [**Birding with Wake Audubon Society**\\ \\ Join our partners at Wake Audubon Society for birding in the Museum Park on the second Saturday morning of each month. Preregistration is required. This program is managed by Wake Audubon. Find more details, register, and direct any questions to them through their Meetup page. Please note: once registered, you will be provided with more information and any updates by Wake Audubon, not the NCMA.\\ \\ November 14, 2026](https://ncartmuseum.org/event/birding-with-wake-audubon-society-5/)
- [**NCMA Dance Gumbo: Dance Fitness with Jordan Farrell**\\ \\ Get moving with this free outdoor dance fitness series. Led by instructor Jordan Farrell, each class blends pop, Zumba, Latin, hip-hop, and more into an energetic, all-levels aerobic workout that celebrates movement, music, and culture in the Museum Park. Photo: Courtesy of the instructor\\ \\ November 14, 2026](https://ncartmuseum.org/event/ncma-dance-gumbo-dance-fitness-with-jordan-farrell-7/)
- [Sold Out\\ \\ **NCMA to Go Art Kits: Sponge, Stamp, Soar / Kit de artedel NCMA para llevar: pinta con esponja, estampa … ¡y a volar!**\\ \\ Get creative with NCMA art and artists at home! Reserve an activity kit with materials for a complete hands-on project plus written instructions. Kits are designed for all ages. In English and Spanish.  This month’s kit provides the materials to explore and play with painting and printing. Create an abstract painting inspired by Helen Frankenthaler’s woodcut print Madame Butterfly.  Image: Helen Frankenthaler, Madame Butterfly, 2000, Woodcut on three sheets of handmade paper from woodblocks carved using traditional ukiyo-e techniques (ed. 32), 41 1/2 × 79 1/2 in., Gift of Mary and Jim Patton ¡Explora tu creatividad en el hogar con el arte y los artistas del NCMA! Reserva un kit de actividades con materiales e instrucciones escritas para un proyecto práctico completo. Los kits se pensaron para personas de todas las edades. Disponibles en inglés y en español. El kit de este mes incluye los materiales para explorar y jugar con pinturas y grabados. Crea una pintura abstracta inspirada en la xilografía de Helen Frankenthaler, Madame Butterfly. Imagen: Helen Frankenthaler, Madame Butterfly, 2000, xilografía de tres hojas de papel hecha a mano sobre grabado en relieve usando las técnicas tradicionales ukiyo-e (ed. 32), 41 1/2 × 79 1/2 pulg., donación de Mary y Jim Patton\\ \\ November 14, 2026](https://ncartmuseum.org/event/ncma-to-go-art-kits-sponge-stamp-soar/)
- [**Audio Description Tour of Ancient Nubia**\\ \\ This audio description tour of Ancient Nubia: Excavating Treasures of the Nile is free with the purchase of an exhibition ticket.  Join us for an expedition into ancient Nubia. Paired with audio description, artifacts to be examined on these tours include monuments, pottery, burial objects, and jewelry representing the Kerma, Napatan, and Meroitic periods. We invite you to get to know ancient Nubia, the sometimes friend, sometimes foe of ancient Egypt.  We welcome and prioritize visitors who are blind, have low vision, or have a learning need that would benefit from an experience that includes AD. Capacity is limited. If you have questions about this accessible tour, please email Molly Hull at mhull@ncartmuseum.org. Image: Nubian artist, Sudan, Winged Isis Pectoral, 538–519 BCE, gold, H. 2 11/16 × W. 6 11/16 in., Harvard University—Boston Museum of Fine Arts Expedition, 20.276; Photo: © Museum of Fine Arts, Boston\\ \\ November 14, 2026](https://ncartmuseum.org/event/audio-description-tour-of-ancient-nubia/)
- [**Still. Moving: LIGHT OF LIFE as Interpreted by Killian Manning**\\ \\ Created in tribute to Yayoi Kusama and inspired by her LIGHT OF LIFE, a work in the NCMA’s People’s Collection, this performance invites audiences into a world where movement, imagery, and storytelling converge. Entitled “killianmanning/noforwardingaddress,” the dance-theater experience draws inspiration from Kusama’s vibrant colors, mesmerizing patterns, and iconic visual language to explore the relationship between the body, the imagination, and the spaces we inhabit. Through dance and theatrical expression, the work offers a living encounter with Kusama’s artistic universe, one that challenges perception, celebrates creative possibility, and invites us to consider how art continues to move us long after we have experienced it. The performance creates a dialogue between the stillness of a work of art and the transformative energy of live performance, illuminating the ways an artist’s vision can be reimagined through the moving body. Featuring George Barrett, Emily Caras, Christina Conley, Gabby Cooper, and Kyle McConaughy. Narrator: Jonathan Leinbach About Still. Moving This performance dance series explores the timeless works of the People’s Collection and loaned works through the lens of movement. Each object becomes a partner in a visual and physical dialogue as dancers interpret form, story, and silence with their bodies. Still. Moving reimagines the gallery as a stage where past and present meet and where the boundaries between objects and experience dissolve.  Image: Yayoi Kusama, LIGHT OF LIFE, 2018, mirrored box and LED lighting system, H. 86 5/8 × W. 84 1/4 × D. 72 7/8 in., Purchased with funds from the North Carolina State Art Society (Robert F. Phifer Bequest) and the bequest of Carlyle Adams, with additional funding from James Keith Brown and Eric Diefenbach, and Dr. W. Kent Davis and Dr. Carlos Garcia-Velez\\ \\ November 14, 2026](https://ncartmuseum.org/event/still-moving-light-of-life-as-interpreted-by-killian-manning/)

[View All](http://ncartmuseum.org/events)

## Members Experience More

Join a community of art enthusiasts across North Carolina and unlock member benefits to make the most of your Museum experience.

[Explore Memberships](https://ncartmuseum.org/memberships/)

### Winston-Salem

One Museum. Two Locations.

The NCMA W-S (formerly the Southeastern Center for Contemporary Art) in Winston-Salem, NC, was founded in 1956 and had been an affiliate of the NCMA since 2007. It was renamed the North Carolina Museum of Art, Winston-Salem, in fall 2023 by the North Carolina Legislature.  

NCMA W-S presents and interprets contemporary art of the United States with programs encompassing the issues engaging artists today.

[Visit Winston-Salem](https://ncmawinstonsalem.gov/)

 Plan Your Visit

 ---

 Whether you're exploring our exhibitions, creating memories with family, or taking a break at Vicky Café, we invite you to experience the Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum as a place of inspiration, connection, and discovery. We are committed to providing every visitor with an exceptional and welcoming experience that sparks curiosity, discovery, and lifelong learning through art. Admission is always free, and the museum is open to all.

 [Visitor Information](https://frost.fiu.edu/visit/index.html 'Click to read visitor information')

 A Smithsonian Affiliate

 ---

 Frost Art Museum proudly offers year-round arts programming that features exhibitions and events as diverse as Miami’s population. As a Smithsonian Affiliate and one of the largest academic art museums in South Florida, we provide the Greater Miami region with free access to international art that spans cultures, disciplines, and art movements.

 [See what's on view](https://frost.fiu.edu/# 'Link to Exhibitions page')

 Digital Collection

 ---

 Frost Art Museum is engaged in an ongoing digitization process to make its collections more accessible to students, faculty, and the larger community. Currently, there are approximately 1,000 images available for viewing. The museum also continues to expand its collection through generous private donations.

## Download the Museum App

## Frost Art Museum–FIU

The Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum is FIU's premier on-campus museum. Since we opened our doors in 2008, the museum has provided the community with free access to world-class art that spans cultures and time periods.

As one of the largest academic museums in South Florida, Frost Art Museum provides FIU students opportunities to engage with art through our exhibitions, collections, internships, and more. While our free educational programming expands access to art for K-12 schools and families in the west Miami-Dade and beyond.

The museum sits on the Avenue of the Arts, near the 107 Avenue entrance to the Modesto A. Maidique Campus.

The Patricia & Phillip Frost Art Museum is proud to be an official Smithsonian Affiliate.

[Link to Smithsonian Affiliate Directory](https://affiliations.si.edu/affiliate-directory/ 'Link to Smithsonian Affiliate Directory')

- ### Support the Parrish

 ## Make A Gift Today

 **The Parrish is for you! Your support makes it all possible.** Please consider making a year-end gift to the Parrish today to sustain the art and community that brings us together. Your 100% tax-deductible donation helps us make art accessible to all.

 [**DONATE NOW**](https://host.nxt.blackbaud.com/adaptive-donor-form?formId=b0a7484b-1e6d-4162-baf6-c60360595274&envid=p-Q_bE5PXjZEiNMK9J9qxKEg&zone=usa)

- Chase Hall, _The Affrilachian Mountains_, 2026. Acrylic and coffee on cotton canvas, pitchfork, shovel, can, coffee canisters, tobacco pouch, and wire. Overall: 96 x 110 x 8 1/2 in. Courtesy of the artist and David Kordansky Gallery. Photography: Christopher Stach.

 ### October 1, 2026–January 25, 2027

 ## On View | FRESH PAINT: Chase Hall

 For the eighth iteration of the collaborative _FRESH PAINT_ exhibition series, the Parrish Art Museum and The FLAG Art Foundation are pleased to present work by artist Chase Hall (American, b. 1993 in St. Paul, Minnesota). For his _FRESH PAINT_ presentation, Hall has created a new painting _The Affrilachian Mountains_ (2026), exhibited for the first time at the Parrish.

- James Brooks (American, 1906–1992). _R-1953_, 1953, oil on canvas, 82 ½ x 89 in. Parrish Art Museum, Water Mill, New York, Gift of JPMorgan Chase, 2021.2.1.

 ### September 26, 2026–February 14, 2027

 ## On View | Abstract Expressionism: The East End, 1940 to Today

 As part of our year-long series _PARRISH USA250: Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness_, this group exhibition examines how the Abstract Expressionist movement flourished and evolved on the East End, highlighting the many voices who contributed to the genre and influenced the styles that followed.

- Robert Indiana (1928–2018), _ONE Through ZERO (The Ten Numbers)_, 1980–2003. Conceived: 1980; Fabricated 2003. Cor-ten Steel on painted aluminum base. Each sculpture: 78 x 74 x 38 in (overall including base). Edition of six plus two artist's proofs. Photo: Liz Glasgow Studios; Artwork: © The Robert Indiana Legacy Initiative/Artists Rights Society (ARS), NY.

 ### July 13, 2026–January 13, 2027

 ## On View | Robert Indiana: ONE Through ZERO (The Ten Numbers)

 Installed in the south meadow at the Parrish Art Museum, _ONE Through ZERO (The Ten Numbers)_ is a sculptural reflection of Robert Indiana’s fascination with the power of numbers. This work has previously exhibited at the Glass House in New Canaan, Connecticut, Chatsworth House in Derbyshire, United Kingdom, and _Robert Indiana: The American Dream_ at Pace Gallery in New York.

- Installation view of _Will Ryman: Shanghai 6_ at the Parrish Art Museum, Water Mill, NY (April 1, 2026–March 31, 2028). Photo: Vision Maker Productions, Inc.

 ### April 1, 2026–March 31, 2028

 ## On View | Will Ryman: Shanghai 6

 _Shanghai 6_ is Will Ryman’s first presentation at the Parrish Art Museum, installed in the Museum’s south meadow. First presented in 2011, through New York City’s Department of Parks and Recreation, the colossal, painted fiberglass, resin, and stainless steel flowers from the on-going _Rose_ series that the artist began fifteen years ago have since been on view on the grounds of museums and private collections across America and abroad.

**For more than two centuries, the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts has played a central role in shaping American art—educating artists, inspiring the public, and preserving cultural history.** Founded in Philadelphia in 1805 as the nation’s first art museum and school, PAFA has evolved alongside changing artistic movements while overcoming challenges and celebrating major milestones. As the United States approaches its 250th anniversary in 2026, PAFA marks its own 220th year by exploring archival stories and key moments that highlight the institution’s long legacy of creativity, resilience, and innovation. [Learn More →](https://www.pafa.org/about/history-pafa/pafa-220-celebrating-220-years)

## Exhibitions & Collections

Experience world-class exhibitions and a nationally recognized permanent collection featuring modern, contemporary, and Indigenous art.

### [Aaron Coleman: Come, Go Back, Child](https://plainsart.org/exhibitions/aaron-coleman/)

Come, Go Back, Child is an exhibition of recent work by multidisciplinary artist Aaron S. Coleman whose art practice examines the entangled histories of race, religion, and power in the United States. Coleman’s densely layered prints, sculptural assemblages, and mixed-media installations explore contemporary Black experiences and critique systems of white supremacy.

- Current

[View Exhibition](https://plainsart.org/exhibitions/aaron-coleman/)

### [Know Your Treaty: Wiwahokichiyapi](https://plainsart.org/exhibitions/know-your-treaty-wiwahokichiyapi/)

Treaties are living documents that are “the supreme law of the land” and remain legally binding agreements that establish the political relationship between Native Nation and the United States government. These agreements have established land boundaries, resource rights, reservations; they determine Tribal Nation citizenship and outline mutual obligations.

- Current

[View Exhibition](https://plainsart.org/exhibitions/know-your-treaty-wiwahokichiyapi/)

### [Threads of Offering](https://plainsart.org/exhibitions/threads-of-offering/)

Thương Hoài Trần (she/they) is an interdisciplinary Vietnamese American artist whose immigrant experience informs their identity and creative practice.

- Current

[View Exhibition](https://plainsart.org/exhibitions/threads-of-offering/)

## The Work is Happening. 
Join the Momentum.

The museum that’s been free is about to become even more welcoming. We’re creating a new welcome center that bonds two beloved buildings into one, new ways to experience more than 6,000 works you’ve never seen, and a commitment to bringing, and sharing art, with future generations. Phase one starts with Collections, a space that has held our work, and now a place you will soon be able to visit.

@graph.description: Plains Art Museum is a free public art institution dedicated to modern, contemporary, and Indigenous visual arts, housing a permanent collection of over 6,000 works alongside rotating world-class exhibitions. Serving as an inclusive creative hub, the museum provides hands-on educational opportunities for all ages, ranging from youth workshops and family programs to adult classes in ceramics, printmaking, and figure drawing, as well as open studio access for community artists.

The Portland Art Museum recognizes and honors the Indigenous peoples of this region on whose ancestral lands the museum now stands.

These include the Willamette Tumwater, Clackamas, Kathlemet, Molalla, Multnomah and Watlala Chinook Peoples and the Tualatin Kalapuya who today are part of the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde, and many other Native communities who made their homes along the Columbia River. We also want to recognize that Portland today is a community of many diverse Native peoples who continue to live and work here. We respectfully acknowledge and honor all Indigenous communities—past, present, future—and are grateful for their ongoing and vibrant presence.

## Welcome Graham C. Boettcher, 
NRM’s New Director and CEO

A message from Graham C. Boettcher, PhD.

August 31, 2026

Today marks an exciting moment for Norman Rockwell Museum as Graham C. Boettcher, PhD, begins his tenure as Director and CEO. On his first day, Graham shares a message of gratitude, connection, and anticipation for the work ahead.

For years, the Museum has brought together art, history, storytelling, and shared experience, inviting visitors to see the world through Norman Rockwell’s legacy and the broader field of illustration. Graham steps into this role following the remarkable tenure of Laurie Norton Moffatt and joins a deeply committed community of staff, board members, volunteers, visitors, members, and supporters who carry the Museum’s mission forward every day.

In the weeks ahead, Graham looks forward to listening, learning, and getting to know the many people who make Norman Rockwell Museum such a special place. He is eager to hear what brings you here, what inspires you, and what hopes you hold for the Museum in the years to come.

“Thank you for welcoming me into this very special community,” Graham shares. “I am excited for the work ahead and grateful to begin this new chapter with you.”

[**Learn More about Graham Here >**](https://www.nrm.org/2026/05/norman-rockwell-museum-appoints-new-director-ceo/)

The Norman Rockwell Museum in Stockbridge, Massachusetts, is the latest home for the  “Exploring Calvin and Hobbes” exhibit, which had a successful run at the Fenimore Art Museum last year. It opens this Saturday, Nov. 14, and runs through May 31, 2027.

- [Rural Intelligence: Rockwell Museum Opens the First Touring Show of “Calvin and Hobbes” Original Drawings](https://www.nrm.org/2026/11/rural-intelligence-rockwell-museum-opens-the-first-touring-show-of-calvin-and-hobbes-original-drawings/)

#### [Rural Intelligence: Rockwell Museum Opens the First Touring Show of “Calvin and Hobbes” Original Drawings](https://www.nrm.org/2026/11/rural-intelligence-rockwell-museum-opens-the-first-touring-show-of-calvin-and-hobbes-original-drawings/)

The Norman Rockwell Museum opens "Exploring Calvin and Hobbes" on Saturday. It is the first touring exhibition built from Bill Watterson’s original drawings, and the museum is the first stop to show it in its entirety. The Billy Ireland Cartoon Library & Museum at The Ohio State University organized the show, curated by Jenny E. Robb. It draws on original daily and Sunday strips and specialty pieces from Watterson’s collection of more than 3,000 originals at the library.

STOCKBRIDGE — Graham Boettcher is very familiar with the responsibilities that come with taking over a cultural institution following the tenure of a long-serving CEO and director.  “I had exactly the same experience in Birmingham. ## Land Acknowledgement

It is with gratitude and humility that we acknowledge that we are learning, speaking and gathering on the ancestral homelands of the Mohican people, who are the indigenous peoples of this land on which the Norman Rockwell Museum was built. Despite tremendous hardship in being forced from here, today their community resides in Wisconsin and is known as the [**Stockbridge-Munsee Community**](https://mohican.com/). We pay honor and respect to their ancestors past and present as we commit to building a more inclusive and equitable space for all.

## _Picasso–Klee–Matisse: Masterpieces from the Museum Berggruen_

Showcasing approximately 100 works by artists such as Alberto Giacometti, Paul Klee, Henri Matisse, and Picasso, _Picasso–Klee–Matisse: Masterpieces from the Museum Berggruen_ invites viewers to encounter Berggruen’s life and vision through a remarkable collection shaped by personal relationships with artists and a deep commitment to modern art.

[Learn More](https://www.pamm.org/en/exhibition/picasso-klee-matisse-masterpieces-from-the-museum-berggruen/)

## _Basquiat: Figures, Signs, Symbols_

Featuring ten masterworks by Jean-Michel Basquiat from the Kenneth C. Griffin Collection, this exhibition is the largest presentation of the artist’s work to date in Florida.

[Learn More](https://www.pamm.org/en/exhibition/basquiat-figures-signs-symbols/)

## _This Is America x PAMMTV_

Centering artist changemakers who reflect the American experience, _This Is America x PAMMTV_ brings together time-based works from PAMM’s permanent collection that examine US politics, the Black American experience, and the role of artists in shaping the nation’s past, present, and future.

[Learn More](https://www.pamm.org/en/exhibition/this-is-america-x-pammtv/)

## New Rollins Museum of Art Facility

Construction is underway for Rollins Museum of Art's new facility coming soon to the heart of Winter Park. View this flyover rendering and click to learn more about this state-of-the-art facility.

[Explore & Give Now](https://www.rollins.edu/rma/new-rma-facility/)

## Free Admission

Located on the [Rollins College](https://www.rollins.edu/) campus, The Rollins Museum of Art features rotating exhibitions, vibrant programming, and **Free Admission** for all. Be sure to also visit our satellite location at [The Alfond Inn](https://www.rollins.edu/rma/the-alfond-inn/) which features 100+ artworks on view from the Rollins Museum of Art Collection.

## Hours

**NEW FALL HOURS!**

**Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday** | 9am-4pm

**Thursday** | 9am-7pm

**Saturday** | 11am-4pm

**Sunday** | 12pm-4pm

Closed Mondays, holidays, and during installations.

[Plan Your Visit](https://www.rollins.edu/rma/visit/)

## Become a Member

Join a dynamic environment where art, ideas, and community unite! Gain access to exclusive opportunities and meaningful engagement not available to the general public.

Join now and secure your membership benefits before the **2028 opening of the** [**new Rollins Museum of Art**](https://www.rollins.edu/rma/new-rma-facility/)—yours to keep with annual renewal, regardless of future level changes.

[Become a Member](https://www.rollins.edu/rma/join/)

## Spotlight

On View Now

### Forging a Legacy: 15 Years of Landmark Acquisitions

May 21, 2026–May 31, 2027

Picasso, Monet, Warhol, and more—Together in one unmissable exhibition.

Explore permanent collection highlights that have enhanced and transformed the Museum’s offerings, creating an enduring legacy of art and inspiration for San Diego. On view are over 120 works from across time and geographies that are a testament to the visionary collecting and the extraordinary generosity of the community over the past 15 years.

[View the Exhibition](https://www.sdmart.org/exhibition/forging-a-legacy-15-years-of-landmark-acquisitions/)

sdma

Pablo Picasso, Femme Assise (detail), 1949. Oil on canvas. Promised Gift of Joan and Irwin Jacobs. © 2026 Estate of Pablo Picasso / Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York.

On View Now

### Cecil Beaton’s Fashionable World

July 11, 2026–January 10, 2027

Photographer, fashion illustrator, Oscar-winning costume designer, social caricaturist, and writer Cecil Beaton (1904–1980) was an extraordinary force in the twentieth-century British and American creative scenes. This is the first exhibition dedicated to Beaton’s fashion and portrait photography, which he elevated into an art form.

[View the Exhibition](https://www.sdmart.org/exhibition/cecil-beatons-fashionable-world/)

Cecil Beaton, The Second Age of Beauty is Glamour, Checked Suit by Norman Hartnell (detail), 1947. Modern print from original colour transparency. © Condé Nast Archive UK.

### Guest Lecture Series

Our monthly series of guest lectures welcomes scholars, artists, authors, and experts from throughout the art world to San Diego for talks that connect a topic to the permanent collection of the Museum and the San Diego arts scene. Lectures are followed by a docent-led tour.

[See the Schedule](https://www.sdmart.org/talks/)

mopa@ 
sdma

### Museum as a Stage

Explore the Museum’s world-renowned collection of art paired with an exciting array of concerts and performances. Museum as a Stage is The San Diego Museum of Art’s performing arts initiative, created to reconnect the performing and visual art traditions and expand the ways audiences experience art. Together with our partners, the Museum transforms into a place where visual and performing arts enrich one another, inviting audiences to encounter art through music, movement, storytelling, and shared cultural celebration.

[See the Performances](https://www.sdmart.org/concerts-and-performances/)

sdma

2026

### SDMA Centennial

Join The San Diego Museum of Art in celebrating 100 years of art, community, and inspiration. Celebrate the Museum’s centennial and visit the Museum throughout 2026 to enjoy groundbreaking exhibitions, dynamic public programs, and unforgettable events that reflect the vibrancy and diversity of our region.

[Join Us](https://www.sdmart.org/centennial/)

sdma

### Visible Vaults

The Visible Vaults recreates part of The San Diego Museum of Art’s most carefully guarded area, a place that is invisible to most visitors—the vaults—where the thousands of works of art in the collection are stored. An insider’s look at hidden masterpieces, visitors are invited to peek into virtual storerooms..

[View the Exhibition](https://www.sdmart.org/exhibition/visible-vaults/)

## The San Diego Museum of Art.

## The San Diego Museum of Art.

The region’s largest and most-visited art museum, The San Diego Museum of Art houses some of the world’s finest art. Located in the heart of Balboa Park, the Museum’s internationally renowned collection of more than 32,000 works dating from 3000 BC to present day. SDMA regularly features major exhibitions of art from around the world, as well as extensive cultural and community experiences that invite visitors to explore art through music, dance, film, food, and so much more.

# San Francisco Museum of Modern Art

## RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me

Be one of the first to see RM's personal collection, featuring many Korean artworks never before exhibited in the US alongside works from SFMOMA’s collection.

Now on View

- [Opening Weekend\\ \\ **New Work: Raven Chacon**\\ \\ Pulitzer Prize–winning composer and artist Raven Chacon’s new commission takes museum visitors on a journey through the vast landscapes of Navajo Nation, reimagined as otherworldly places in a speculative future.](https://www.sfmoma.org/exhibition/new-work-raven-chacon/)
- [Now on View\\ \\ **Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc**\\ \\ Blending sculpture and environment, Jacob Hashimoto has transformed SFMOMA’s Roberts Family Gallery into a mesmerizing, floating cloudscape of nearly 75,000 hand-crafted kites.](https://www.sfmoma.org/exhibition/jacob-hashimoto-giant-arc/)

## Get art delivered to your inbox

[Sign Me Up](https://sfmoma.prospect2.com/f/4)

[Now On View\\ \\ **Graciela Iturbide: Between Two Worlds**\\ \\ This expansive survey of the Mexico City–based artist’s black-and-white photographs immerses viewers in Iturbide’s visual world of uncanny scenes and dreamlike traditions.](https://www.sfmoma.org/exhibition/graciela-iturbide-between-two-worlds/)

- [Art for All\\ \\ **Families and Kids**\\ \\ Guests 18 and younger always get in for free at SFMOMA! Learn more about our variety of family programs and resources.](https://www.sfmoma.org/for-families/)
- [Membership\\ \\ **Join Our Community**\\ \\ Enjoy first access to exhibitions, free admission for you and a guest, and other exclusive offerings.](https://www.sfmoma.org/membership/)

- [Museum Store\\ \\ **Tucker Nichols x SFMOMA**\\ \\ Brighten your day with colorful, only-at-SFMOMA merchandise featuring the dreamy florals and quirky San Francisco–inspired sentiments of Tucker Nichols.](https://museumstore.sfmoma.org/collections/tucker-nichols-x-sfmoma)
- [Read\\ \\ **RM x SFMOMA: A Private Collection of Korean Art Revealed**\\ \\ Preview the first museum exhibition featuring paintings, drawings, sculptures, ceramics, textiles, and design works from the personal collection of RM, leader of pop royalty BTS.](https://www.sfmoma.org/read/rm-x-sfmoma-a-private-collection-of-korean-art-revealed/)

# Welcome to the San Antonio Museum of Art

Come see the world, be inspired.

[Buy Tickets](http://50182a.blackbaudhosting.com/50182a/tickets?tab=3&txobjid=8bfcb27b-bd72-4e78-bfdd-6f73be1f8909) [Memberships](https://www.samuseum.org/membership/)

## See the World

Explore 5,000 Years of Art, People, and Culture

A visit to the San Antonio Museum of Art (SAMA) takes you around the world and through five thousand years of art in a complex of buildings that once housed the Lone Star Brewery. SAMA is renowned for the most comprehensive ancient Greek, Roman, and Egyptian art collection in the southern United States. The Nelson A. Rockefeller Latin American art wing spans the ages from the ancient Americas to the present and includes an outstanding collection of popular art. In the contemporary galleries, works of internationally recognized artists share prominence with notable Texas and regional art. The comprehensive Asian art wing displays works from Korea, India, and Japan, and includes an important Chinese ceramics collection.

[View Collections](https://www.samuseum.org/artwork/browse-the-collection/)

Enjoy unlimited Museum and Special Exhibition admission, exclusive member events, and a 10% discount in the Museum Shop and Restaurant.

The dog has a front-row seat. So do we. 

In #JennaGribbon’s "I am the dog" (2023), sweeping curtains, monumental scale, and dramatic lighting borrow from the grandeur of heroic painting. An exposed curtain rod and clamp light reveal how the scene has been staged. 

Gribbon’s wife, a performer herself, actively shapes the portrait through her pose and gestures. In the foreground, the family dog becomes a stand-in for both the artist and us, drawing our attention to our own role as onlookers. The painting makes visible a collaboration between two people who understand the power of making an image together. 

See "I am the dog" in "Jenna Gribbon: Entwined" at the Rose Art Museum.

[Favorites 30](https://www.instagram.com/p/DfuelwYCBcf/) [Comments 3](https://www.instagram.com/p/DfuelwYCBcf/)

1 day ago

“It’s a struggle not to project yourself onto your child,” #JennaGribbon has remarked. 

That thought takes visible form in two paintings brought into dialogue in "Jenna Gribbon: Entwined." In "A Reflection Held" (2024), at left, Gribbon’s reflected image appears beside her son’s face. In "My face on his face (warm)" (2024), on the right, her likeness is projected onto his, their features overlapping in glowing color. 

Together, these double portraits explore the complicated emotions of watching a child grow: wanting to preserve a profound bond while making room for independence. Reflection and projection become ways of considering how a parent sees a child, recognizes herself in him, and learns to let him become his own person. 

Spend time with both paintings in "Jenna Gribbon: Entwined" at the Rose Art Museum. 

\_\_\_\_\_\_ 
Installation view, "Jenna Gribbon: Entwined," Rose Art Museum, Brandeis University, August 19, 2026–January 3, 2027. Julia Featheringill Photography.

In a pas de deux, two dancers move in response to each other while remaining distinct. #JennaGribbon brings that exchange into "Pas de Deux" (2026), where traces of her own face emerge within her wife’s features. 

Gribbon has described her wife as a “kind of proxy” for herself. Here, painting someone she loves becomes a way of exploring her own identity. Her wife remains unmistakably herself, even as the portrait suggests how deeply our understanding of ourselves can be shaped by another person. 

Swipe through the details to follow these overlapping likenesses, then see "Pas de Deux" in "Jenna Gribbon: Entwined" at the Rose Art Museum. 

\_\_\_\_\_\_ 
Jenna Gribbon, "Pas de Deux," 2026. Oil on linen. Photography: Christopher Stach. Courtesy of the artist and Lévy Gorvy Dayan. © Jenna Gribbon.

A second perspective can change what you see. 

In "Jenna Gribbon: Entwined," relationships shape the paintings and the experience of looking at them. Gribbon’s depictions of the people closest to her invite us to consider how we see and understand one another. Exploring the galleries with someone else offers its own discoveries: a detail you missed, a different interpretation, a connection you hadn’t considered. 

Bring a friend to the Rose Art Museum, take your time, and compare notes. 

\_\_\_\_\_\_ 
Installation view, "Jenna Gribbon: Entwined," Rose Art Museum, Brandeis University, August 19, 2026–January 3, 2027. Photo by @FrancoisVisuals.

What does sanctuary mean in a world shaped by conflict, displacement, and questions of belonging? 

On Thursday, December 10, hear directly from internationally acclaimed artist #YinkaShonibare in a special virtual conversation with Gannit Ankori, Henry and Lois Foster Director and Chief Curator of the Rose Art Museum. 

Known for his striking use of color, theatricality, and wit, Shonibare has spent his career exploring histories of colonialism, cultural identity, and power. Together, Shonibare and Ankori will discuss the ideas behind his groundbreaking practice and Sanctuary City (2024), an immersive installation of 18 illuminated architectural models representing places of refuge across the globe. 

As "Yinka Shonibare: Sanctuary" prepares to leave the Rose for a national tour, this is a special opportunity to hear from the artist about the histories, inspirations, and urgent questions at the heart of his work. 

📅 In Conversation: Yinka Shonibare 
Thursday, December 10 | Virtual 

Free and open to all! Register through the link in our bio.

Spend time with "Jenna Gribbon: Entwined." 

Bringing together more than 40 paintings made over two decades, the exhibition traces Gribbon’s evolving approach to portraiture through images of family, friends, lovers, and herself. Across the galleries, scale shifts dramatically, perspectives overlap, and familiar relationships become sites of experimentation, memory, and discovery. 

Experience Gribbon’s first major museum survey in person at the Rose. 

"Jenna Gribbon: Entwined" is on view through January 3, 2027. 

Plan your visit at the link in bio.
